title: podman image rm - concurrent with shared layers: build fails unpacking its own layer
body:
`podman image rm - concurrent with shared layers` has gone red 9 times between 2026-06-08 and 2026-08-12, on five different distro and mode combinations, so it does not look environmental:

```
5x  int local root fedora-rawhide
1x  int local rootless fedora-rawhide
1x  int local rootless fedora-current
1x  int local rootless debian-sid
1x  int remote root debian-sid
```

The failure is in the build half of the test, not the removal half. The assert that fires is `buildImage()` in common_test.go, and the reason is only on stderr, so the TAP line alone shows a build that ran to COMMIT and exited 1:

```
Error: committing container for step {... Args:[touch rmtest:0] ...}: copying layers and
metadata for container "04c35a38...": writing blob: adding layer with blob "sha256:724a7a77...":
unpacking failed (error: exit status 1; output: open /rmtest:0: no such file or directory)
```

`unpacking failed` comes from `invokeUnpack` in c/storage `pkg/chrootarchive/archive_unix.go`, and the quoted output is what the `storage-untar` re-exec child printed. The child gets the destination as an fd (`/proc/self/fd/4`) and creates entries under it, so an ENOENT while creating `/rmtest:0` reads like the destination went away underneath it rather than the tar being wrong. The test starts ten builds in goroutines off the same base image, which is what makes it concurrent.

The job had composefs and partial images on:

```
--storage-opt overlay.use_composefs=true
--pull-option=enable_partial_images=true --pull-option=convert_images=true
```

I have not reproduced it locally, and I did not get further than the error above, so I do not know which side removes the directory.

#18659 covered the same test being racy but is closed and locked, and that one was about the removal half.

comments.body:
found the mechanism, though not the culprit yet. the untar child chroots into the destination, and a directory that is unlinked while you are chrooted into it keeps working for anything already open but fails every create with ENOENT:

```
create BEFORE removal :  OK
create AFTER  removal :  No such file or directory   (errno 2)
```

so `open /rmtest:0: no such file or directory` means the destination went away mid unpack, not that the layer tar is bad. I reproduced the exact string locally by removing the destination partway through an unpack.

what still removes it during this test I do not know. opened podman-container-tools/container-libs#1115 so the error at least says which of the two it is next time.

I'm encountering similar issues when running multiple image builds/pulls concurrently on the same machine using Podman 6.0 (also had these issues with older Podman versions). I'm not entirely sure if this is related but the logs I encountered so far:
```
Error: committing container for step {Env:[PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin:/usr/local/bun-node-fallback-bin BUN_RUNTIME_TRANSPILER_CACHE_PATH=0 BUN_INSTALL_BIN=/usr/local/bin NODE_ENV=production] Command:copy Args:[. .] Flags:[] Attrs:map[] Message:COPY . . Heredocs:[] Original:COPY . .}: copying layers and metadata for container "970a42039af223b390d22bb7939ea52f9e0b933f5aef57cc7b00a6221dacc480": writing blob: adding layer with blob "sha256:1eef7d34c79e05e6b0c89d2fab4aa7f07f711255d8f4587b1761fa516a9aa489"/""/"sha256:22220d5b068ab239be493a1ac4ef510af293209824dfa06d9b1360a1b27e2fb2": unpacking failed (error: exit status 1; output: mkdir /app: no such file or directory)
```

```
unable to copy from source docker://<snip>/dockerhub/library/postgres:16: copying system image from manifest list: writing blob: adding layer with blob "sha256:00034b17b963695ef825816fbf4147c71f32b66d5c0743dcaee4c4711e8ba8b6"/""/"sha256:428818b3d4fc4a3e4ca1be4f71a5a96c31b1a8ee8cf6797b31e09d82b143107f": rename /home/runner/.local/share/containers/storage/overlay-layers/tmp/temp-dir-896991578/0-addition /home/runner/.local/share/containers/storage/overlay-layers/d123591175e99fc8c2c21a8b0f92327ee4ff4e7b7ed4ad31bfecdcfcb8608395.tar-split.gz: no such file or directory
```

I have seen this before in the logs but never had the time to dive deep, it seem to be kinda rare. If it end users hit this as well it is certainly worth to spend some more time on it.

I think the fact that the destination directory gets removed in the untar case is most likely and does not really need more special cases/debug code.

The interesting question is of course which process deletes these files, is the tmpdir setup not locked properly?
I can try to revive my bpftracer on the new CI system and log all file path removals matching that pattern. 


> Podman 6.0 (also had these issues with older Podman versions)

This code path was only added in podman 5.8 so I doubt you have seen that with versions older than that at least.

@Luap99 on "is the tmpdir setup not locked properly", I think there is a window in the staging lock, before you spend time on bpftrace.

`CreateAndLock` creates the lock file and locks it as two separate steps (c/storage internal/staging_lockfile/staging_lockfile.go):

```go
file, err := os.CreateTemp(dir, pattern)   // lock file exists now, not locked
file.Close()
path := file.Name()
l, err := tryAcquireLockForFile(path)      // locked only here
```

and `NewTempDir` locks first, then makes the directory, so the ordering there is right.

the problem is what another process does in that gap. `listPotentialStaleDirs` collects ids from lock prefixed entries as well as temp-dir prefixed ones, so `RecoverStaleDirs` sees the brand new lock file, and `TryLockPath` succeeds on it because the creator has not locked it yet. It then removes the temp dir and, worse, `UnlockAndDelete()` removes the lock file.

after that the creator makes its temp dir with no lock file guarding it, and `TryLockPath` creates the file if it is missing, so the next `RecoverStaleDirs` locks it and deletes a directory that is in active use.

`RecoverStaleDirs` runs on layer store load, so anything doing concurrent pulls or builds hits it constantly, which fits @eplightning seeing it outside CI.

I have not reproduced this, it is from reading the code, so treat it as a lead rather than a conclusion. the untar case would be the same thing one level up.

> the problem is what another process does in that gap. listPotentialStaleDirs collects ids from lock prefixed entries as well as temp-dir prefixed ones, so RecoverStaleDirs sees the brand new lock file, and TryLockPath succeeds on it because the creator has not locked it yet. It then removes the temp dir and, worse, UnlockAndDelete() removes the lock file.

I don't read it that way. Even if RecoverStaleDirs wins and locks/delete the file the tmpdir is not yet created and TryLockPath will either fail to lock it in which case the CreateAndLock should retry with a new name or it can lock it in which case we hold the lock and RecoverStaleDirs should skip it or in case it already passed over it NewTempDir will create the dir only once the lock is being held so it cannot be removed after this.

youre right @Luap99 , I walked the interleavings again and the protocol holds.

I also checked the other direction, whether Cleanup could run before commitLayer, but m.cleanup() is deferred in PutLayer so it runs after. so I do not have a mechanism, the bpftrace is probably the way.
